title: BEAM: Bi-level Memory-adaptive Algorithmic Evolution for LLM-Powered Heuristic Design

parentSelection: Adjacent rank-based crossover; elitist mutation with best-individual guidance

mechanism.domainTask: Bi-level LLM design of complete heuristic algorithms and low-level function implementations
mechanism.populationDetail: The exterior GA evolves a ranked population of complete algorithm individuals; no islands or maintained search tree are described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate archive of complete candidate algorithms is specified; AM stores reusable functions extracted from elite individuals, not whole solutions.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Next-generation individuals are selected/educated from parents plus crossover and mutation offspring; the worst are eliminated at the configured population limit. AM separately inserts/replaces/evicts function components.
mechanism.generationDetail: The exterior layer crosses two adjacent quality-ranked structures and mutates one structure using the best individual as guidance; MCTS separately searches function realizations within each structure.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: AM uses function fitness, novelty, usage, age, and recent improvement statistics for admission, replacement, eviction, and pruning.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Crossover pairs consecutive quality-ranked individuals; mutation applies to a current individual and is guided by the best heuristic.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Bi-level search separates complete-algorithm structural evolution from MCTS-based function realization and maintains an adaptive memory of reusable function components.
